subject: Merchant Labs: sudden request backlog & throughput degradation — urgent
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@merchantlabs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Merchant Labs SRE <sre@merchantlabs.com>
Date: 2025-11-09T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Checkout failures & p99 spikes during peak - need immediate help

Ben / Marissa,

We started seeing severe user-facing errors on Sunday morning during our peak (09:00–10:30 PST). Symptoms: p95 stayed OK (~350ms) but p99 shot to ~9–12s, error rate for completions jumped to ~2.8% (previous baseline ~0.1%), and overall throughput dropped by ~30% even while traffic was flat. This is impacting checkout confirmations — we had ~120 failed orders in one hour.

We captured a perf snapshot and a trace (attached). Merchant Labs SRE sees a buildup of requests in the Redwood router queues and a lot of retries from our side. The problem appears to coincide with a change in concurrency throttling you deployed last week (you reduced per-tenant concurrency caps). We need an urgent mitigation: can you open an incident and either lift caps temporarily or route our traffic to a less-loaded pool? We are open to a quick call.

Short summary of impact:
- Customer-facing errors: checkout timeouts/failures
- p99: 9–12s during 09:00–10:30 PST window
- Error spike: ~2.8%
- Throughput drop: ~30%

Attaching: perf_snapshot_20251109.png, request-trace-1109.json

Samir
OPS / Merchant Labs

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@merchantlabs.com>, Merchant Labs SRE <sre@merchantlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-09T09:28:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures & p99 spikes during peak - need immediate help

Samir — thanks for the data and the quick heads-up. I’m really sorry for the disruption. I’ve stood up an incident and looped in engineering (Dylan) and our customer success lead (Marissa).

Immediate plan (next 30 minutes):
- Engineering to triage queue/backpressure and propose an immediate mitigation (Dylan)
- If safe, we can raise your per-tenant concurrency cap and enable a short-term burst policy to relieve queued requests
- If rerouting is required, we’ll move traffic to a backup pool in a different region/zone (expected ~5–10m to switch)
- Marissa will coordinate customer comms and decide whether to offer temporary credits; we’ll avoid premature promises until we have a root-cause readout

I’ll host a quick call at 09:45 PST to align on action. Dylan — can you confirm earliest mitigation and what logs/traces you need?

Ben
SR. ACCOUNTS / Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Merchant Labs SRE <sre@merchantlabs.com>
Date: 2025-11-09T09:40:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Checkout failures & p99 spikes during peak - need immediate help

On Sun, Nov 9, 2025 at 09:12 AM Samir Patel <samir@merchantlabs.com> wrote:
> We started seeing severe user-facing errors...

Short diagnosis after initial triage: we’re seeing request queueing at the front-end router and uneven KV-cache hot keys that are causing head-of-line blocking. The recent conservative adjustment to per-tenant concurrency caps (rolled out last week) reduced headroom; when Merchant Labs’ traffic had a bursty pattern with long token sequences, it pushed a subset of workers into backpressure and other requests accumulated in the router queue.

Immediate mitigation I recommend (can do in the next 10–20 minutes):
1) Increase per-tenant concurrency cap from 80 -> 160 for Merchant Labs. This will allow currently queued requests to drain.
2) Enable a temporary per-tenant burst window (60s) so they can exceed cap briefly to clear backlog.
3) Toggle prefix/KV caching to aggressive mode for their model-family (reduces repeated prefix compute).
4) If queueing persists, reroute traffic to our backup pool (gcp-us-east1) and shift a small % of traffic incrementally for canary.

Risks: raising caps temporarily increases tail CPU/GPU usage and may change cost profile; we’ll monitor closely and revert when stable. We have traces attached (request-trace-1109.json) — they show worker-side token serialization and requeueing.

I’ll implement 1–3 now and watch metrics; Ben, please confirm and give green light for reroute if needed.

—Dylan
Platform Reliability Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@merchantlabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Checkout failures & p99 spikes during peak - need immediate help

Samir — I’m on the call with your SREs and have passed a short note to your Ops channel. We appreciate the attachments; please stand by while Dylan applies the mitigations.

Customer comms suggestion: we’ll frame this as a temporary capacity constraint caused by a combination of a recent throttle change + atypical sequence lengths. We’ll offer real-time status updates every 15 minutes and follow up with a post-mortem timeline.

Customer asks I’ll need to escalate to leadership:
- Are we prepared to offer a short-term credit for impacted orders if we can confirm failures were caused by our service?
- If the customer asks for a permanent higher cap, we’ll need a billing / contract addendum (DocuSign).

Ben — please advise on compensation band and whether to open a formal exec note request. Samir — I’ll update you as soon as Dylan confirms drain.

Marissa

Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Checkout failures & p99 spikes during peak - need immediate help

Thanks team. Ben/Marissa — please prepare a concise exec brief for revenue leadership if this will cross the SLA threshold. I prefer we avoid upfront credits until we have a confirmed RCA and impact quantification, but we should be ready with an approval band (e.g., X% credit for orders impacted between time A and B) to move quickly.

Needed for brief:

- p99/p95 and error-rate delta vs baseline
- Total # of impacted user requests / failed checkouts
- Proposed immediate compensation band (if any) and rationale
- Mitigation steps taken and ETA to normal

If this turns into an ongoing capacity request from Merchant Labs, work with Sales Ops to draft an SLA amendment and present pricing. Keep me posted.

Karthik
Head of Sales — Accounts

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@merchantlabs.com>, Merchant Labs SRE <sre@merchantlabs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-11T16:44:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident update & next steps — Merchant Labs (11/09/2025)

Samir / Elena / SREs —

Thank you again for your patience. This is a short summary of what we did and the next steps: 

What happened:
- Root cause: the per-tenant concurrency cap combined with a small set of hot KV-key workloads produced head-of-line blocking and router queueing during a burst of long-sequence requests. This produced p99 spikes (9–12s) and an error-rate increase as requests timed out/retried.

Immediate remediation applied (11/09, 09:45–10:10 PST):
- Raised Merchant Labs per-tenant concurrency cap from 80 to 160 and enabled a 60s burst window.
- Aggressive prefix/KV caching enabled for the model family in use.
- Rerouted 25% of traffic to our backup pool (gcp-us-east1) as a canary; after validation we moved remaining traffic.
- Monitored for two business days. Metrics returned to baseline p99 (~400ms) and error rate fell back to ~0.12% within ~45 minutes of mitigations.

Customer impact numbers we’re using in the exec brief:
- Degradation window: 2025-11-09T09:02:00-08:00 -> 2025-11-09T10:38:00-08:00
- Peak p99: 9–12s; baseline p99: ~400ms
- Estimated failed checkouts: 120 (Merchant Labs data)

Next steps / preventative changes:
1) Engineering will roll a targeted fix to reduce head-of-line blocking by improving KV cache locality and request prioritization (ETA: one week).
2) We’ll add an adaptive per-tenant cap algorithm for bursty patterns (ETA: two weeks).
3) Ops/CS to offer a targeted compensation band; Marissa, please propose wording. I’ve attached a draft DocuSign amendment if Merchant Labs requests a permanent higher cap.

Samir — if you’re comfortable, please confirm acceptance of the temporary mitigation and whether you’d like us to initiate the DocuSign SLA amendment for a permanent cap increase. Apologies for the disruption — we will share a written post-mortem once the engineering fix is validated.

Attachments: DocuSign-SLA-Amendment-draft.pdf, perf_snapshot_20251109.png

Ben Carter
SR. ACCOUNTS / Redwood Inference
